title: Russian-installed authorities hold referendums on joining Russia in four occupied regions of Ukraine
body:
From 23 to 27 September 2022, Russian-installed officials held votes on joining Russia in occupied parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. Voting also took place in Russia. Many commentators called the votes sham referendums. Reports described armed soldiers going door to door to collect ballots, and voting was restricted to specific people until the final day.

Russian election officials reported the following results. Donetsk: 99.23 percent in favour, with 97.51 percent turnout. Luhansk: 98.42 percent in favour, with 94.15 percent turnout. Kherson: 87.05 percent in favour, with 76.86 percent turnout. Zaporizhzhia: 93.11 percent in favour, with 85.4 percent declared turnout.

The UN Secretary-General said the votes violated the UN Charter. Ukraine, the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany and many other countries rejected the results. North Korea was the only state reported to accept them. On 30 September 2022 Vladimir Putin announced the annexation of the four regions. On 12 October 2022 the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution ES-11/4, which declared the referendums and the attempted annexation invalid. The vote was 143 in favour, 5 against and 35 abstentions, with 10 members absent.
